**Brazil and ECB explore linking Pix to euro instant payments**

*Technical teams are studying whether Brazil's Pix could interconnect with the euro area's TARGET Instant Payment Settlement infrastructure, in what would be the first direct link between two domestic instant payment schemes across continents.*

Brazil's central bank and the ECB are in early-stage discussions about connecting Pix – Brazil's instant payments system – to TARGET Instant Payment Settlement (TIPS), the euro area's instant settlement infrastructure, according to Reuters. Technical teams on both sides are assessing the feasibility of a direct link, though no formal agreement has been reached.

A Pix-TIPS connection would represent a different model from the correspondent banking and hub-based approaches that have dominated cross-border instant payments to date. Rather than routing through intermediaries, it would aim to establish scheme-to-scheme interoperability – a concept the Bank for International Settlements has championed but which has seen limited real-world implementation. Brazil handles more than 5 billion Pix transactions per month; TIPS has been scaling rapidly as the EU's instant payments regulation takes effect.

The initiative sits alongside other cross-border instant payment efforts, including the ECB's recent launch of cross-currency settlement between the euro area, Denmark and Sweden, and the commercially oriented mBridge project backed by China. A successful Pix-TIPS link would extend the ECB's cross-border ambitions well beyond the European neighbourhood and give euro area banks a direct corridor into Latin America's largest economy.

*Sources: [Brazil, ECB studying instant payments link in potential first cross-border move for Pix, sources say](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazil-ecb-studying-instant-payments-link-potential-first-cross-border-move-pix-2026-09-03/) — Reuters | [Brazil, ECB Studying Instant Payments Link in Potential First Cross-Border Move for Pix, Sources Say](https://ground.news/article/bc-negotiates-to-link-pix-to-the-european-payment-system-02-09-2026) — Ground | [Brazil's Pix Could Link Up With The ECB's Instant Payments](https://finimize.com/content/brazils-pix-could-link-up-with-the-ecbs-instant-payments) — Finimize*

**Mollie completes GoCardless acquisition to form pan-European payments group**

*The €1.1bn deal closes five months after announcement, combining Mollie's merchant acquiring with GoCardless's account-to-account collections to create a combined platform spanning card, pay-by-bank and recurring payments.*

Mollie has completed its acquisition of GoCardless, finalising a transaction first announced earlier this year. The deal brings together Mollie's European merchant payment processing with GoCardless's direct debit and account-to-account collections infrastructure, creating a group with coverage across card acceptance, open banking payments and recurring bank mandates.

GoCardless, founded in London in 2011, built its business on bank-to-bank payment collection and had reached profitability in the first quarter of the current financial year. Mollie, headquartered in Amsterdam, processes payments for more than 250,000 European merchants. The combined entity positions itself as a multi-rail alternative for European businesses that have typically relied on separate providers for card acquiring and account-to-account payments.

The completion follows a broader wave of consolidation across European payments, including Nordic Capital's merger of Qred and Liberis, and NMI's acquisition of Dwolla. The deal's logic reflects a market view that merchants increasingly want a single provider capable of routing transactions across cards, instant payments and direct debits – a proposition that becomes more compelling as open banking payment volumes grow.

*Sources: [Mollie Closes On Acquisition Of UK Fintech GoCardless](https://www.crowdfundinsider.com/2026/09/305461-mollie-closes-on-acquisition-of-uk-fintech-gocardless/) — Crowdfund Insider*

**FCA explores using rent payment data in mortgage affordability checks**

*The regulator is examining how open finance could allow rental payment histories to count toward mortgage eligibility, extending the logic of the FCA's existing open banking affordability work into housing.*

The Financial Conduct Authority is exploring whether rental payment histories could be incorporated into mortgage affordability assessments using open finance data. The initiative would allow prospective borrowers who have consistently paid rent on time to have that record reflected in lending decisions – a change that could particularly benefit first-time buyers who lack traditional credit histories.

The FCA signalled in June that open banking data would reshape mortgage affordability checks. Incorporating rent payments extends that direction by treating regular housing expenditure as evidence of creditworthiness, an approach that consumer advocates and housing groups have long pushed for but which has lacked a practical data-sharing mechanism.

Open finance infrastructure makes the proposal technically feasible: with borrower consent, lenders could access verified transaction data showing rent payments directly from bank accounts, bypassing the need for landlord references or manual proof. The challenge lies in standardisation – rent payments vary in format, timing and labelling across bank statements – and in ensuring that the data is used to widen access rather than to impose additional scrutiny on applicants.

*Sources: [FCA explores rent payments as mortgage evidence](https://mortgagesoup.co.uk/fca-explores-rent-payments-as-mortgage-evidence/) — Mortgagesoup*

**India blocks Alipay+ link to instant payments system on security grounds**

*Growing caution about allowing foreign platforms access to domestic real-time payment rails has led Indian authorities to stall Alipay+'s proposed connection to UPI.*

India has stalled a proposal by Alipay+ to connect with the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), the country's dominant instant payments system, citing national security and data sovereignty concerns. The move blocks what would have been one of the most significant cross-border instant payment integrations in Asia.

Alipay+, operated by Ant International, already facilitates cross-border merchant payments in multiple Asian markets by connecting local payment methods to its platform. A UPI link would have given Alipay+ access to a system that processes more than 18 billion transactions per month and serves as the backbone of India's digital payments infrastructure. Indian authorities are understood to have concerns about data flows to China-linked entities and the potential for a foreign platform to gain systemic importance within domestic payment infrastructure.

The decision contrasts with the ECB's willingness to explore cross-border instant payment links – including the newly reported Pix–TIPS discussions – and highlights the geopolitical fault lines emerging in real-time payments interoperability. India's stance offers a reference point for European policymakers weighing their own approach to foreign platform access under PSD3 and the digital euro framework, where similar questions about security concerns and interoperability ambitions are in play.

*Sources: [NEWS: India stalls Alipay+ payments link over security and data concerns](https://www.amlintelligence.com/2026/09/news-india-stalls-alipay-payments-link-over-security-and-data-concerns/) — AML Intelligence*
